chapter: Hometown ties, community and favorite players
title: Best small bands: Kid Rena and Henry Hardin
summary: Kid Rena's small band, and Jones's time with Henry Hardin.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Uh huh. What about small bands? Were there any good small bands there? Back in the thirties? Uh huh.

Kid Rainy. He had a small band, a lot of small bands, but Rainy and Joe Robichaud had the finest small band. He had the greatest band he had in the late years. Cause he had a drummer by the name of Bucket, he had Porter, he had Gene Ware, Gene Hall,
Gene Ware on trumpet. And Joe on piano. And he had a banjo player by the name of Walter, that's the last, I forgot Walter's other name, but he went to New York.
Didn't Henry Hardin have a band then? Yeah.

I worked with Henry Hardin. I worked with Henry Hardin with Alvin's brother, George McCullough. Uh huh. With the first trumpet player. Gilbert Young was the second trumpet player. Russell's third trumpet player.
We had a saxophone player named Edward Bodley. You heard of him? Yeah, I heard of him.
And uh, Fosche, what you call him? Earl? Well Fosche. Yeah. A piano player? Well we called him the Gopher, Benny, we had William Benny. Mm-hm.
